answer: Each agent earns influence only by completing a sequence of escrowed tasks with distinct, randomly assigned peers; a deposit is slashed when a peer proves collusion or fabricated delivery. Because identities alone cannot create task history, an attacker must fund many agents, keep them active, and coordinate credible work without triggering cross-checks. Quartz, nectar, and onyx can label task categories, but the defense comes from costly, verifiable participation, not from the labels themselves.
